context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at scale while enabling manual analyst reviews. It ensures low-latency decisions, strict PCI-DSS compliance, and tamper-evident auditing within a fixed budget and small team.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems
- Fraud Scoring Engine (AWS ECS/Lambda)
- Case Management SaaS
- Third-Party Fraud Intelligence Feeds
- Identity Provider (AWS Cognito / Okta)
- Decision Audit Store (AWS S3 Object Lock & AWS KMS)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to Fraud Scoring Engine via gRPC/HTTPS for low-latency requests
- Fraud Scoring Engine to Third-Party Fraud Intelligence Feeds via HTTPS
- Fraud Scoring Engine to Case Management SaaS via secure REST APIs/Webhooks
- Fraud Scoring Engine to Audit Store via asynchronous log streaming with AWS KMS signing

## Technology Stack
- AWS eu-west-1: Target cloud region ensuring compliance and low latency
- Terraform/CDK: Infrastructure-as-code for zero-downtime deployments and GitOps
- AWS S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): Write-once-read-many storage for 7-year auditability
- AWS KMS: Cryptographic signing for tamper-evident decision logs
- gRPC / HTTPS: High-performance protocols for core scoring evaluation

## Rationale
The architecture separates high-throughput synchronous scoring from asynchronous case management to meet the P99 latency SLA. Offloading UI components to SaaS and utilizing managed AWS services ensures PCI-DSS compliance and operational feasibility for a three-person engineering team.

API Gateway & Routing Layer.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations and case management for fraud analysts. It evaluates transactions under strict latency and compliance constraints.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems
- API Gateway & Routing Layer (AWS ALB + AWS WAF)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate, Go/Java, ONNX Runtime)
- Analyst & Rules Portal (AWS Amplify / S3 + CloudFront)
- Case Management Backend (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Audit & Event Stream (Amazon SQS / EventBridge + Kinesis Data Firehose)
- Decision Audit Store (AWS S3 Object Lock & AWS KMS)
- Identity Provider (AWS Cognito / Okta)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Acquirer Systems -> API Gateway & Routing Layer: Sends payment authorization requests [HTTPS/JSON via mTLS]
- API Gateway & Routing Layer -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes authorization payloads for scoring [gRPC / HTTP2 over AWS VPC private links]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Decision Audit Store: Persists decisions, inputs, and model versions [AWS KMS / HTTPS]
- Analyst & Rules Portal -> Case Management Backend: Manages suspicious payment reviews [HTTPS/JSON via OAuth2/JWT]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ALB + AWS WAF: Edge routing, TLS 1.3 termination, rate-limiting, DDoS protection, and PCI-DSS PAN masking without per-request cost penalties.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration for microservices, eliminating server management for a 3-engineer team.
- Amazon S3 Object Lock & AWS KMS: Tamper-evident storage ensuring 7-year auditability and compliance.
- gRPC / HTTP2: Internal communication protocol guaranteeing P99 latency below 50 ms at 3,000 TPS.

## Rationale
This architecture uses fully managed AWS services to minimize operational toil for a three-engineer team while respecting the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. It meets strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability requirements via secure edge tokenization and tamper-evident storage.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
This system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time while providing a portal for fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms latency, PCI-DSS compliance, and zero-downtime model updates within a fixed cloud budget.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate, Go/Java, ONNX Runtime)
- Rule Evaluation Component (Go + expr-lang/expr)
- ML Inference Component (ONNX Runtime C++ bindings wrapped in Go)
- Decision Orchestrator Component
- Rule Compiler & Validator Component
- API Gateway & Routing Layer (AWS API Gateway / ALB)
- Audit & Event Stream (Amazon SQS / EventBridge + Kinesis Data Firehose)
- Decision Audit Store (AWS S3 Object Lock & AWS KMS)

## Relationships
- API Gateway & Routing Layer -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Routes authorization payloads for scoring [mTLS / HTTPS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Audit & Event Stream: Streams scoring decisions and audit events [Amazon SQS / EventBridge]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Third-Party Fraud Intelligence Feeds: Queries external threat intelligence [AWS PrivateLink]
- Rule Evaluation Component & ML Inference Component -> AWS S3: Hot-reloads models and rules atomically via S3 polling/notifications [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration for cost-effective, serverless scaling within budget
- Go: High-performance language chosen for low memory overhead and sub-50ms latency
- ONNX Runtime: Optimized machine learning inference engine for fast model execution
- expr-lang/expr: Lightweight evaluation engine for fast in-memory fraud rule execution
- AWS S3 & KMS: Encrypted object storage with strict IAM controls for tamper-evident 7-year audit compliance

## Rationale
The architecture combines Go and ONNX Runtime on serverless AWS ECS Fargate to consistently deliver sub-50ms P99 decision latencies at high throughput. In-memory components, atomic S3 hot-reloading, and robust validation ensure continuous availability and seamless PCI-DSS compliance within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Analyst & Rules Portal.analysis:
## Overview
The Analyst & Rules Portal provides a secure React-based interface for analysts and risk managers to review suspicious payment cases and configure fraud rules. It operates on AWS CloudFront and S3 while adhering to PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- SPA Frontend Core (React/TypeScript, Recharts, AWS S3, CloudFront)
- Case Review UI Module
- Rule Authoring & Simulation Module
- Simulation Results Visualizer
- AWS WAF & Amazon SQS
- Identity Provider (AWS Cognito/Okta)

## Relationships
- Manual Analyst -> SPA Frontend Core via HTTPS [OIDC/OAuth2]
- Merchant Risk Manager -> SPA Frontend Core via HTTPS [OIDC/OAuth2]
- Rule Authoring & Simulation Module -> Amazon SQS via JSON [AWS SDK]
- SPA Frontend Core -> Case Management Backend via REST/HTTPS
- SPA Frontend Core -> Identity Provider via OIDC/OAuth2 [PKCE flow]

## Technology Stack
- React/TypeScript: Lightweight SPA framework for fast frontend delivery by a three-engineer team.
- AWS S3 & CloudFront: Cost-effective static hosting with global CDN delivery.
- Recharts/Chart.js: Minimal bundle-size charting library for rendering simulation impact metrics.
- Amazon SQS: Asynchronous queue to safely decouple heavy rule-backtesting jobs from frontend requests.
- AWS WAF: Edge security to protect authentication endpoints from brute-force attacks.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict security, PCI compliance, and user requirements while operating within a fixed 25,000 EUR monthly budget and three-engineer team limit. Asynchronous simulation queuing and memory-only token storage prevent resource starvation and data-exfiltration risks.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Backend processes fraud review workflows for payment analysts using an isolated, scalable microservice architecture. It provides high-performance REST/GraphQL APIs and asynchronous bulk processing while maintaining strict PCI-DSS compliance and auditability.

## Key Elements
- Case API Controller (AWS ECS Fargate, Node.js/Express/Fastify)
- Workflow Engine Component (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Batch Processing Worker Component (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Notification & Telemetry Component (Node.js/TypeScript)
- Audit Dispatcher Component (Node.js/TypeScript)
- PostgreSQL Database (AWS RDS with AWS KMS encryption)
- Asynchronous Job Queue (Amazon SQS / Redis on Amazon ElastiCache with DLQ)

## Relationships
- Analyst & Rules Portal -> Case API Controller: Submits REST/GraphQL requests [HTTPS/REST/GraphQL]
- Case API Controller -> Asynchronous Job Queue: Enqueues bulk requests [AWS SQS / Redis protocol]
- Batch Processing Worker Component -> Workflow Engine Component: Executes state transitions [In-process function calls]
- Workflow Engine Component -> PostgreSQL Database: Persists case state [PostgreSQL wire protocol over TLS 1.3]
- Audit Dispatcher Component -> Audit & Event Stream: Streams immutable audit events [Amazon EventBridge]
- Notification & Telemetry Component -> Analyst & Rules Portal: Pushes job status updates [WebSockets]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration ensuring serverless operational simplicity for a 3-engineer team.
- Node.js & TypeScript: Runtime and language for rapid API development with strict schema validation (Zod/Joi).
- AWS RDS PostgreSQL: Relational storage for transactional case states, protected via AWS KMS and AWS Secrets Manager.
- Amazon SQS / Redis: Asynchronous job queuing preventing gateway timeouts during bulk decisioning.
- AWS X-Ray & CloudWatch: Distributed tracing and monitoring enforcing system observability.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict 7-year auditability and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance with a fixed €25k monthly budget through serverless scaling and managed AWS services. Separating real-time APIs from batch workers protects database performance, ensuring rapid analyst workflows under heavy transaction loads.

Audit & Event Stream.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect and prevent fraud before approval, while providing case management for manual reviews. It ensures strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year immutable auditability within a strict infrastructure budget and small engineering team.

## Key Elements
- **Manual Analyst**: Human user reviewing suspicious payments via the frontend portal.
- **Real-Time Scoring Engine**: Container executing fraud models via AWS ECS Fargate and ONNX Runtime.
- **Audit & Event Stream**: Container ingesting, buffering, and dispatching compliance and decision events.
- **Event Ingestion Router**: Amazon EventBridge component routing schema-validated events.
- **Buffer & Batcher**: Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose component aggregating events into Parquet batches.
- **Decision Audit Store**: External system using AWS S3 Object Lock and AWS KMS for 7-year tamper-evident storage.

## Relationships
- **Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Event Ingestion Router**: Streams scoring decisions and explainability metadata via HTTPS / EventBridge `PutEvents` API.
- **Case Management Backend -> Event Ingestion Router**: Streams case workflow events via HTTPS / EventBridge `PutEvents` API.
- **Event Ingestion Router -> Buffer & Batcher**: Forwards filtered events via Kinesis Firehose direct integration over HTTPS.
- **Buffer & Batcher -> Decision Audit Store**: Delivers encrypted Parquet batches via S3 API over TLS 1.3.

## Technology Stack
- **AWS EventBridge**: Used for serverless, decoupled event ingestion and routing with Dead Letter Queues to minimize operational overhead.
- **AWS Kinesis Data Firehose**: Used to batch and compress high-throughput events into Parquet format within budget.
- **AWS S3 Object Lock & KMS**: Used for 7-year tamper-evident audit log retention and encryption in Compliance Mode.
- **AWS CDK**: Used for infrastructure-as-code definition by a three-person engineering team.

## Rationale
Serverless AWS components eliminate self-hosted infrastructure management, fitting the three-engineer team limit and 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Asynchronous event streaming ensures sub-50ms P99 scoring latency while satisfying strict PCI-DSS and 7-year auditability requirements.
